## CEO BRIEFING

**State of play as of 14:20 UTC**

- We have an open incident on the **Batch API only**. Errors began at **11:42**. We applied a mitigation at **12:58** and error rates fell immediately to near baseline. The service is recovering and under close monitoring.
- **It is not resolved.** Our policy requires 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate before we can declare resolution. That window closes at **14:30** — i.e. ten minutes from now, and after your board call begins. I will come back to you the moment it closes with a clean or not-clean answer.
- **Root cause is not established.** Two candidate explanations are still live and neither has been tested. At 12:31 we deliberately decided *not* to roll back the suspect release, because rolling back would have destroyed the evidence we need to test it. I stand by that call, but it means I cannot give you a cause today.
- **Residual risk:** until the affected infrastructure is returned to service, all Batch traffic is running on a single fleet with no failover. That is the thing most likely to bite us in the next few hours. It is being managed, not ignored.

**Impact — use these numbers**

- **58,900** Batch API requests between 11:42 and 12:58. **17,602** failed with 5xx. **29.9%** — this is the headline figure and the only one to quote.
- **7 of our 9 Batch API accounts** were affected; 2 were not. The other 27 accounts don't use Batch and were never exposed.
- For scale: we served **842,000** requests platform-wide in the same window, so Batch is roughly 7% of traffic. This is a contained failure, not a platform event.
- Symptom was 502 errors on batch job submission. Submissions were partially succeeding throughout — it was never a hard outage. Inference, Embeddings and Files were healthy the whole time.

**Contoso**

- Contoso is the **only affected account whose contract carries service credits**, and they have asked twice today, including directly about Schedule B credits.
- **Do not commit to a credit and do not confirm a breach.** Their contract calculates Monthly Availability across all Covered Services, after month end, from our records, published within 10 business days — with a 30-day claim window after that. The November figure cannot be known on 9 November. That is the answer, and it is a complete answer.
- If pushed: their schedule excludes requests that failed due to customer retry behaviour exceeding rate limits, and Contoso has an open, acknowledged retry-without-backoff issue from last week. Any exclusion must be itemised with its basis and is disputable. I am not asserting an exclusion — only that one may apply.

**If it comes up on the board call**

Say: contained to the Batch API; mitigation applied at 12:58; service recovering under monitoring; recovery confirmation expected this afternoon; root-cause analysis underway; one enterprise account engaged through the contractual SLA process.

Do not say: "resolved" or "fixed"; "root cause identified" or any speculation about cause; any credit amount or confirmation of breach; any completion time for the root-cause work or for returning the affected infrastructure to service.

**Watch-out — the public record is currently wrong**

Our 12:05 status page update said we had identified the cause and expected full restoration within the hour. That was premature; Marcus stopped further cause statements at 12:09. We are publishing a correction now that withdraws the cause claim. If anyone on the board has looked at the status page, that is the context — better you raise it than they do.

**One unrelated item — not for the board**

While triaging, Marcus found a standing over-permission on a batch worker database role (read/write on the billing schema, which it has no reason to touch). It played no part in this incident. Ticket SEC-411, Marcus owns it, targeted this week. Confidential and Northstar-internal — flagging so you are not blindsided later, but please do not raise it.

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

**INC-2026-1109-01 — 14:20 UTC — handover**

**Status: OPEN, mitigated, verification in progress, root cause not established.** I am handing this to the on-call chain now. Verification window closes **14:30** — ten minutes.

### What happened

`batch-api@2026.11.09-r3` finished rolling out to both fleets at 11:31 (three dependency bumps; worker DB connection-pool max lowered 80 → 24 per worker). fleet-a volume climbed from 11:38 to ~3x the morning average, driven by wonka-industries starting a large scheduled job. First page 11:42: 502s on `POST /v1/batch/jobs`, confined to fleet-a. fleet-b clean throughout. Upstream object-storage provider ruled out at 11:47 (provider status green, Files API on the same provider healthy).

At 12:31 we decided **not** to roll back r3 — a rollback would remove the evidence needed to test whether the pool change is responsible. Mitigated instead by cutting all Batch traffic to fleet-b at **12:58**. fleet-a drained and held out of rotation. Error rate fell to 0.4% within two minutes (baseline 0.2%); 0.3–0.4% since. No new customer failures reported since cutover.

### Impact (from `customer-impact.csv`, internal)

| Account | Requests | Failures | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| stark-industries | 14,200 | 5,180 | 36.5% |
| contoso | 9,400 | 3,410 | 36.3% |
| wayne-enterprises | 7,850 | 2,790 | 35.5% |
| globex | 6,100 | 2,240 | 36.7% |
| wonka-industries | 5,900 | 2,020 | 34.2% |
| umbrella-health | 4,300 | 1,560 | 36.3% |
| initech | 1,150 | 402 | 35.0% |
| **All affected** | **48,900** | **17,602** | **36.0%** |
| acme-corp | 6,700 | 0 | 0% |
| aperture-labs | 3,300 | 0 | 0% |
| **All Batch API** | **58,900** | **17,602** | **29.9%** |

**External reporting figure is 29.9%** (failed Batch requests ÷ all Batch requests). Fleet membership is an internal deployment detail and is **not** a reporting basis — do not quote the 36.0% fleet-a figure externally.

### Root cause — three propositions, none tested

- **H1 — connection-pool change in r3 (leading).** For: pool lowered 80→24 at 11:31, eleven minutes before first page; workers observably queueing on DB connections. Against: r3 is on fleet-b too and fleet-b never degraded.
- **H2 — concentrated load on fleet-a (secondary, live).** For: ~3x morning average from 11:38, one large scheduled job. Against: fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.
- **H1×H2 interaction** — a lower pool ceiling biting under higher concurrency. This is a third proposition, not a conclusion.
- H3 (upstream storage) — rejected at 11:47.

**Analytical note, worth carrying forward:** failure rates are tightly clustered at 34–37% across all seven affected accounts *regardless of account size* — initech, at 1,150 requests, failed at essentially the same rate as stark at 14,200. That points to a fleet-wide shared resource rather than any individual account's volume, which is consistent with a connection-pool ceiling. It does **not** distinguish H1 from H1×H2. Do not treat it as a finding.

### Open items and owners

1. **14:30 — verification close (Priya, Marcus).** Confirm the 90-minute window closed clean. Also explicitly confirm that 0.3–0.4% against a 0.2% baseline satisfies "normal error rate" under the policy — I want that stated, not assumed. No resolution statement before this.
2. **Re-drive (Priya).** ~60% complete at 13:52, no failures on re-drive. Finish it and report completion. Failed jobs are being replayed for affected accounts.
3. **Rollback test (Marcus).** Not run. fleet-a is drained, so it is now a zero-customer-traffic test bed. Reproduce with r3 in place vs rolled back, under the 11:38 load profile, and settle H1 vs H2 vs interaction. This is the blocking item for root cause.
4. **fleet-a return to rotation (Marcus).** Do **not** return it as-is. Recurrence risk is real and we currently have no failover. Define the return criteria first.
5. **Status page (Ruth).** Correction publishing now; next public update committed for **14:45**. Anything published comes from Tomas's approved list only. The 12:05 "Identified" post is wrong and is being withdrawn.
6. **Support (Tomas) — four live threads:** Contoso (TKT-8903/8907 — impact figures plus SLA process, no credit commitment); umbrella-health (TKT-8904 — compliance export due today, needs a substantive reply); wonka-industries (TKT-8912 — asking whether to resubmit or whether we replay; we are replaying, so confirm the no-duplicate-resubmission guidance before it goes out); globex (TKT-8918 — they think they were unaffected; they were, 2,240 of 6,100 failed; Tomas to correct that).

### For whoever picks this up

- Do not use the words "fixed," "resolved," or "root cause identified" in any channel, internal or external, until Marcus confirms and the 14:30 window has closed clean.
- Do not roll back r3 on any serving fleet without Marcus — it destroys the test evidence.
- Marcus's rough planning estimate for full wrap and fleet-a back in rotation is ~16:00 if the window closes clean and the re-drive completes. **That is his personal internal estimate, explicitly not for anyone outside this channel** — do not put it in a status page, a customer email, or the CEO briefing.
- The 12:31 decision not to roll back is a deliberate, recorded decision. If you are challenged on it, the rationale is evidence preservation while customers were made whole by the cutover.

### Confidential — not part of this incident

While reading fleet-a worker config, Marcus found the batch worker's DB role holds read **and write** on the billing schema, which it has no reason to touch. **No part in this incident, not a contributing factor.** Standing over-permission, should have been caught in review. **SEC-411**, Marcus owns, targeted this week to narrow to read-only on the two tables actually used. Restricted to Northstar staff — do not paste this section into any customer-facing or status channel, and do not add it to the incident write-up distribution.

## CUSTOMER EMAIL

**To:** Contoso
**Subject:** Re: Batch submits failing / Service credits — incident INC-2026-1109-01

Hello,

Thank you for your two messages today (TKT-8903 and TKT-8907), and for offering Priya Raghunathan as a technical contact — we have that noted and will use it if it becomes useful.

**What happened to you**

We have had an incident affecting the Batch API. It began at **11:42 UTC today**. During it, a portion of batch job submissions returned 502 errors.

Your account's figures for the incident window (11:42–12:58 UTC) are:

- Batch API requests: **9,400**
- Requests returning an error: **3,410** (36.3%)
- First failure: **11:43 UTC**
- Last failure: **12:56 UTC**

**Where we are now**

A mitigation was applied at **12:58 UTC**. Error rates have returned to near baseline and the service is recovering. We are monitoring before we confirm full recovery — **this incident is not yet resolved**, and I do not want to tell you otherwise until we can stand behind it.

I will send you a further update by **15:30 UTC today**, whether or not we have been able to confirm full recovery by then. In the meantime our public status page will be updated by 14:45 UTC.

**Service credits under Schedule B**

I cannot confirm today whether November will breach the 99.9% commitment, and I am not going to guess at it. Under B.2 and B.5, Monthly Availability is calculated per calendar month across the Covered Services from our own service records **after the end of the month**, and we publish the figure within 10 business days of month end. You then have 30 days from that publication to submit a credit claim, with credits following the B.4 table.

Two points so there are no surprises later. First, the B.2 exclusions apply to that calculation — including B.2(b) and (c) covering requests that failed as a result of customer-side integration or retry behaviour exceeding documented rate limits. You flagged last week that a backoff change to your integration is queued behind your Q4 freeze; we are not asking you to change anything now, but I want to be straightforward that it is relevant to how the monthly figure is computed. Second, where any volume is excluded under B.2(b), B.6 requires us to identify the excluded volume and the basis for it in the published figure, and you may dispute that exclusion within the claim window.

**On the impact data above:** these are the raw failure counts for your account in the incident window. They are not the B.2 calculation and they do not by themselves establish a credit entitlement.

Again, I am sorry for the disruption. We will be back to you by 15:30 UTC today.

Kind regards,
Northstar Support
Incident INC-2026-1109-01

## STATUS PAGE UPDATE

**2026-11-09 14:20 — Batch API: mitigation applied, monitoring**

We are continuing to respond to the incident affecting the Batch API, which began at **11:42 UTC** today.

A mitigation was applied at **12:58 UTC**. Error rates on batch job submission have returned to near baseline and the service is recovering. We are monitoring before we confirm full recovery — **this incident is not yet resolved.**

Our other APIs — Inference, Embeddings and Files — are unaffected, and have been throughout.

**Correction to our 12:05 update.** That update stated that we had identified the cause of these errors and expected full restoration within the hour. That was premature. We have **not** confirmed a root cause, and we will not publish anything further about cause until we have.

We will post our next update by **14:45 UTC**.

*Monitoring.*
